passages.text: When Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem the Arab, and the rest of our enemies heard that I had rebuilt the wall and not a gap was left—though to that time I had not yet installed the doors in the gates— Sanballat and Geshem sent me this message: “Come, let us meet together in one of the villages on the plain of Ono.” But they were planning to harm me.
passages.sermon:
Nehemiah was the governor of Jerusalem.
He led the people to rebuild the city wall.
Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem the Arab, and the rest of our enemies heard about the wall.
They heard that I had finished rebuilding the wall.
There was no gap left in the wall.
At that time, I had not yet put the doors in the gates.
Sanballat and Geshem sent a message to me.
They said, “Come, let us meet together in one of the villages on the plain of Ono.”
They planned to harm me.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֣י כַאֲשֶׁ֣ר נִשְׁמַ֣ע לְסַנְבַלַּ֣ט וְ֠טוֹבִיָּה וּלְגֶ֨שֶׁם הָֽעַרְבִ֜י וּלְיֶ֣תֶר אֹֽיְבֵ֗ינוּ כִּ֤י בָנִ֙יתִי֙ אֶת־ הַ֣חוֹמָ֔ה וְלֹא־ נ֥וֹתַר בָּ֖הּ פָּ֑רֶץ גַּ֚ם עַד־ הָעֵ֣ת הַהִ֔יא דְּלָת֖וֹת לֹא־ הֶעֱמַ֥דְתִּי בַשְּׁעָרִֽים׃ וַיִּשְׁלַ֨ח סַנְבַלַּ֤ט וְגֶ֙שֶׁם֙ אֵלַ֣י לֵאמֹ֔ר לְכָ֞ה וְנִֽוָּעֲדָ֥ה יַחְדָּ֛ו בַּכְּפִירִ֖ים בְּבִקְעַ֣ת אוֹנ֑וֹ וְהֵ֙מָּה֙ חֹֽשְׁבִ֔ים לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת לִ֖י רָעָֽה׃

passages.text: So I sent messengers to them, saying, “I am doing a great work and cannot come down. Why should the work stop while I leave it to go down to you?”
passages.sermon:
Nehemiah was the leader rebuilding Jerusalem’s wall.
Enemies tried to distract Nehemiah from his work.
Nehemiah sent messengers to his enemies.
He told them, “I am doing a great work.”
He said, “I cannot come down.”
He asked, “Why should the work stop while I leave it?”
He said, “I will not go down to you.”
passages.original: וָאֶשְׁלְחָ֨ה עֲלֵיהֶ֤ם מַלְאָכִים֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר מְלָאכָ֤ה גְדוֹלָה֙ אֲנִ֣י עֹשֶׂ֔ה וְלֹ֥א אוּכַ֖ל לָרֶ֑דֶת לָ֣מָּה תִשְׁבַּ֤ת הַמְּלָאכָה֙ כַּאֲשֶׁ֣ר אַרְפֶּ֔הָ וְיָרַדְתִּ֖י אֲלֵיכֶֽם׃

passages.text: Four times they sent me the same message, and each time I gave the same reply.
passages.sermon:
Sanballat and Geshem were enemies of the Jews.
They wanted to harm me, Nehemiah, who was leading the rebuilding of Jerusalem’s wall.
They sent me a message.
They asked me to meet them.
They sent this same message four times.
Each time, I gave them the same answer.
I refused to meet them.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלְח֥וּ אֵלַ֛י כַּדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּ֖ה אַרְבַּ֣ע פְּעָמִ֑ים וָאָשִׁ֥יב אוֹתָ֖ם כַּדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּֽה׃ס

passages.text: The fifth time, Sanballat sent me this same message by his young servant, who had in his hand an unsealed letter that read: “It is reported among the nations—and Geshem agrees—that you and the Jews are plotting to revolt, and this is why you are building the wall. According to these reports, you are to become their king, and you have even appointed prophets in Jerusalem to proclaim on your behalf: ‘There is a king in Judah.’ Soon these rumors will reach the ears of the king. So come, let us confer together.”
passages.sermon:
Sanballat was an enemy of Nehemiah and the Jews.
Sanballat sent a message to Nehemiah for the fifth time.
Sanballat sent his young servant to deliver the message.
The servant carried an unsealed letter in his hand.
The letter said that people among the nations had heard a report.
Geshem also agreed with this report.
The report said that Nehemiah and the Jews were planning to rebel.
The report said this was the reason Nehemiah was building the wall.
The report said Nehemiah wanted to become king over the Jews.
The letter said Nehemiah had appointed prophets in Jerusalem.
These prophets were to announce, “There is a king in Judah.”
The letter warned that these rumors would soon reach the king.
The letter invited Nehemiah to come and meet together with Sanballat.
passages.original: וַיִּשְׁלַח֩ אֵלַ֨י סַנְבַלַּ֜ט כַּדָּבָ֥ר הַזֶּ֛ה פַּ֥עַם חֲמִישִׁ֖ית אֶֽת־ נַעֲר֑וֹ וְאִגֶּ֥רֶת פְּתוּחָ֖ה בְּיָדֽוֹ׃ כָּת֣וּב בָּ֗הּ בַּגּוֹיִ֤ם נִשְׁמָע֙ וְגַשְׁמ֣וּ אֹמֵ֔ר אַתָּ֤ה וְהַיְּהוּדִים֙ חֹשְׁבִ֣ים לִמְר֔וֹד עַל־ כֵּ֛ן אַתָּ֥ה בוֹנֶ֖ה הַחוֹמָ֑ה וְאַתָּ֗ה הֹוֶ֤ה לָהֶם֙ לְמֶ֔לֶךְ כַּדְּבָרִ֖ים הָאֵֽלֶּה׃ וְגַם־ נְבִיאִ֡ים הֶעֱמַ֣דְתָּ לִקְרֹא֩ עָלֶ֨יךָ בִֽירוּשָׁלִַ֜ם לֵאמֹ֗ר מֶ֚לֶךְ בִּֽיהוּדָ֔ה וְעַתָּה֙ יִשָּׁמַ֣ע לַמֶּ֔לֶךְ כַּדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֑לֶּה וְעַתָּ֣ה לְכָ֔ה וְנִֽוָּעֲצָ֖ה יַחְדָּֽו׃ס

passages.text: Then I sent him this reply: “There is nothing to these rumors you are spreading; you are inventing them in your own mind.”
passages.sermon:
Nehemiah was the governor of Judah.
Sanballat accused Nehemiah of planning a revolt.
Sanballat spread false rumors about Nehemiah.
Nehemiah sent a reply to Sanballat.
Nehemiah said, “These things you say are not true.”
Nehemiah said, “You are making them up in your own mind.”
passages.original: וָאֶשְׁלְחָ֤ה אֵלָיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר לֹ֤א נִֽהְיָה֙ כַּדְּבָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה אֲשֶׁ֖ר אַתָּ֣ה אוֹמֵ֑ר כִּ֥י מִֽלִּבְּךָ֖ אַתָּ֥ה בוֹדָֽאם׃

passages.text: For they were all trying to frighten us, saying, “Their hands will be weakened in the work, and it will never be finished.” But now, my God, strengthen my hands.
passages.sermon:
Many people opposed us.
They tried to make us afraid.
They said, “Their hands will become weak in the work.
The work will not be finished.”
But now, my God, make my hands strong.
passages.original: כִּ֣י כֻלָּ֗ם מְיָֽרְאִ֤ים אוֹתָ֙נוּ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר יִרְפּ֧וּ יְדֵיהֶ֛ם מִן־ הַמְּלָאכָ֖ה וְלֹ֣א תֵעָשֶׂ֑ה וְעַתָּ֖ה חַזֵּ֥ק אֶת־ יָדָֽי׃

passages.text: Later, I went to the house of Shemaiah son of Delaiah, the son of Mehetabel, who was confined to his house. He said: “Let us meet at the house of God inside the temple. Let us shut the temple doors because they are coming to kill you— by night they are coming to kill you!”
passages.sermon:
Nehemiah was a leader rebuilding Jerusalem’s wall.
Shemaiah was the son of Delaiah and the grandson of Mehetabel.
Shemaiah was confined to his house.
I went to Shemaiah’s house.
Shemaiah spoke to me.
He said, “Let us meet at the house of God.”
He said, “Let us go inside the temple.”
He said, “Let us shut the temple doors.”
He said, “They are coming to kill you.”
He said, “They are coming to kill you at night.”
passages.original: וַאֲנִי־ בָ֗אתִי בֵּ֣ית שְֽׁמַֽעְיָ֧ה בֶן־ דְּלָיָ֛ה בֶּן־ מְהֵֽיטַבְאֵ֖ל וְה֣וּא עָצ֑וּר וַיֹּ֡אמֶר נִוָּעֵד֩ אֶל־ בֵּ֨ית הָאֱלֹהִ֜ים אֶל־ תּ֣וֹךְ הַֽהֵיכָ֗ל וְנִסְגְּרָה֙ דַּלְת֣וֹת הַהֵיכָ֔ל כִּ֚י בָּאִ֣ים לְהָרְגֶ֔ךָ וְלַ֖יְלָה בָּאִ֥ים לְהָרְגֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: But I replied, “Should a man like me run away? Should one like me go into the temple to save his own life? I will not go!”
passages.sermon:
Nehemiah was a leader rebuilding Jerusalem’s wall.
Enemies tried to frighten him.
They wanted him to stop the work.
Shemaiah told Nehemiah to hide in the temple to save his life.
Nehemiah answered him.
Nehemiah said, “Should a man like me run away?”
Nehemiah said, “Should someone like me enter the temple to save his own life?”
Nehemiah said, “I will not go.”
passages.original: וָאֹמְרָ֗ה הַאִ֤ישׁ כָּמ֙וֹנִי֙ יִבְרָ֔ח וּמִ֥י כָמ֛וֹנִי אֲשֶׁר־ יָב֥וֹא אֶל־ הַהֵיכָ֖ל וָחָ֑י לֹ֖א אָבֽוֹא׃

passages.text: I realized that God had not sent him, but that he had uttered this prophecy against me because Tobiah and Sanballat had hired him.
passages.sermon:
Nehemiah was the leader rebuilding Jerusalem’s wall.
Nehemiah realized something important.
God had not sent Shemaiah.
Shemaiah spoke a prophecy against Nehemiah.
Tobiah and Sanballat hired Shemaiah.
Shemaiah acted because they paid him.
passages.original: וָאַכִּ֕ירָה וְהִנֵּ֥ה לֹֽא־ אֱלֹהִ֖ים שְׁלָח֑וֹ כִּ֤י הַנְּבוּאָה֙ דִּבֶּ֣ר עָלַ֔י וְטוֹבִיָּ֥ה וְסַנְבַלַּ֖ט שְׂכָרֽוֹ׃

passages.text: He had been hired to intimidate me so that I would sin by doing as he suggested, so they could give me a bad name in order to discredit me.
passages.sermon:
Tobiah and Sanballat hired this man.
They wanted him to frighten me.
They hoped I would become afraid.
They wanted me to do what he said.
If I did this, I would sin.
They wanted to give me a bad name.
They wanted to shame me.
They wanted to discredit me.
passages.original: לְמַ֤עַן שָׂכוּר֙ ה֔וּא לְמַֽעַן־ אִירָ֥א וְאֶֽעֱשֶׂה־ כֵּ֖ן וְחָטָ֑אתִי וְהָיָ֤ה לָהֶם֙ לְשֵׁ֣ם רָ֔ע לְמַ֖עַן יְחָֽרְפֽוּנִי׃פ

passages.text: O my God, remember Tobiah and Sanballat for what they have done, and also Noadiah the prophetess and the other prophets who tried to intimidate me.
passages.sermon:
Nehemiah was a leader of the Jews who rebuilt Jerusalem’s wall.
Tobiah and Sanballat were his enemies.
They tried to stop Nehemiah’s work.
Noadiah was a prophetess.
Other prophets also opposed Nehemiah.
Nehemiah prayed to God.
He said, “My God, remember Tobiah and Sanballat for what they have done.”
He also said, “Remember Noadiah the prophetess.”
He said, “Remember the other prophets who tried to intimidate me.”
passages.original: זָכְרָ֧ה אֱלֹהַ֛י לְטוֹבִיָּ֥ה וּלְסַנְבַלַּ֖ט כְּמַעֲשָׂ֣יו אֵ֑לֶּה וְגַ֨ם לְנוֹעַדְיָ֤ה הַנְּבִיאָה֙ וּלְיֶ֣תֶר הַנְּבִיאִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֥ר הָי֖וּ מְיָֽרְאִ֥ים אוֹתִֽי׃

passages.text: So the wall was completed in fifty-two days, on the twenty-fifth of Elul.
passages.sermon:
Nehemiah led the people of Jerusalem.
They rebuilt the city wall.
They finished the wall in fifty-two days.
They completed the work on the twenty-fifth day of the month of Elul.
passages.original: וַתִּשְׁלַם֙ הַֽחוֹמָ֔ה בְּעֶשְׂרִ֥ים וַחֲמִשָּׁ֖ה לֶאֱל֑וּל לַחֲמִשִּׁ֥ים וּשְׁנַ֖יִם יֽוֹם׃פ

passages.text: When all our enemies heard about this, all the surrounding nations were afraid and disheartened, for they realized that this task had been accomplished by our God.
passages.sermon:
Our enemies heard about the wall being finished.
The nations around us saw what happened.
These nations became very afraid.
They lost their confidence.
They understood something important.
They realized our God had done this work.
passages.original: וַיְהִ֗י כַּאֲשֶׁ֤ר שָֽׁמְעוּ֙ כָּל־ א֣וֹיְבֵ֔ינוּ וַיִּֽרְא֗וּ כָּל־ הַגּוֹיִם֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר סְבִֽיבֹתֵ֔ינוּ וַיִּפְּל֥וּ מְאֹ֖ד בְּעֵינֵיהֶ֑ם וַיֵּ֣דְע֔וּ כִּ֚י מֵאֵ֣ת אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ נֶעֶשְׂתָ֖ה הַמְּלָאכָ֥ה הַזֹּֽאת׃

passages.text: Also in those days, the nobles of Judah sent many letters to Tobiah, and Tobiah’s letters came back to them.
passages.sermon: The nobles of Judah lived at that time.\r\nThese nobles sent many letters to Tobiah.\r\nTobiah sent letters back to the nobles of Judah.
passages.original: גַּ֣ם׀ בַּיָּמִ֣ים הָהֵ֗ם מַרְבִּ֞ים חֹרֵ֤י יְהוּדָה֙ אִגְּרֹ֣תֵיהֶ֔ם הוֹלְכ֖וֹת עַל־ טוֹבִיָּ֑ה וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר לְטוֹבִיָּ֖ה בָּא֥וֹת אֲלֵיהֶֽם׃

passages.text: For many in Judah were bound by oath to him, since he was a son-in-law of Shecaniah son of Arah, and his son Jehohanan had married the daughter of Meshullam son of Berechiah.
passages.sermon:
Many people in Judah had made an oath to Tobiah.
Tobiah was the son-in-law of Shecaniah.
Shecaniah was the son of Arah.
Jehohanan was Tobiah’s son.
Jehohanan married the daughter of Meshullam.
Meshullam was the son of Berechiah.
passages.original: כִּי־ רַבִּ֣ים בִּֽיהוּדָ֗ה בַּעֲלֵ֤י שְׁבוּעָה֙ ל֔וֹ כִּי־ חָתָ֥ן ה֖וּא לִשְׁכַנְיָ֣ה בֶן־ אָרַ֑ח וִֽיהוֹחָנָ֣ן בְּנ֔וֹ לָקַ֕ח אֶת־ בַּת־ מְשֻׁלָּ֖ם בֶּ֥ן בֶּֽרֶכְיָֽה׃

passages.text: Moreover, these nobles kept reporting to me Tobiah’s good deeds, and they relayed my words to him. And Tobiah sent letters to intimidate me.
passages.sermon:
The nobles of Judah spoke to me about Tobiah’s good deeds.
They told me what Tobiah had done.
They also told Tobiah what I said.
Tobiah sent letters to frighten me.
passages.original: גַּ֣ם טוֹבֹתָ֗יו הָי֤וּ אֹמְרִים֙ לְפָנַ֔י וּדְבָרַ֕י הָי֥וּ מוֹצִיאִ֖ים ל֑וֹ אִגְּר֛וֹת שָׁלַ֥ח טוֹבִיָּ֖ה לְיָֽרְאֵֽנִי׃
